messages:
Alana: seeing a p95 bump on a small subset of Llama3-13B traffic after the recent kernel selector tweak. only affects chat flows with short system prompts. :thinking:
Matt: ugh, numbers?
Alana: p50 ~12ms unchanged, p95 from 120ms -> 260ms. tail looks correlated with KV eviction churn + falling back to slow matmul path. repro trace attached (flamegraph id fg-37455).
Matt: can you paste the selector logs? maybe it chose the fused L2L3 kernel for weird head_dim combos.
Alana: here, minimal snippet from selector: `selected_kernel=fused_l2l3`, `head_dim=96`, `hidden_size=12288`, `rope_theta_scale=1.0`, `kv_cache_hits=low`. That combination is expected to be fast, but when KV cache miss rate > 40% we see extra memcpy + kv-rebuild overhead.
Kai: interesting — our batching heuristic prefers the fused kernel when sequence lengths are uniform and >64. Short chat templates (system + 1 user turn) end up with small prefix lengths and the runtime still picks fused path because of average_sequence heuristic.
Jess: that matches what I saw in QA. Many chat templates insert a long-system prompt only for some customers; for others the system prompt is tiny so sequence distribution is bimodal. Canary traffic had mixed templates.
Alana: repro profile (short):
```
# flamegraph summary
hotspots: fused_matmul (42%), kv_rebuild (23%), memcpy (12%), rmsnorm (6%)
obs: memcpy spikes align with kernel switch paths
```
Matt: RMSNorm/SiLU cost looks fine. The big delta is kv_rebuild + memcpy. Could be that fused kernel's memory layout expects contiguous KV or different striding and we pay expensive transforms on miss.
Kai: proposed quick fixes:
- change selector to prefer non-fused kernel when `kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.6`
- add per-model `rope_theta` metadata so selector doesn't assume default scaling across variants
- tweak batching: prefer `max_batch_tokens` cap so small-chat flows get coalesced instead of triggering dedicated fused path
Jess: + investigate chat template tagging so the router attaches `chat_template=short|long` metadata to requests. then kernel policy can use that.
Alana: my local test: flipping selector rule reduced p95 back to ~130ms, p50 unchanged. Patch diff below:
```
- if avg_seq_len > 64 and heads==96: choose fused
+ if avg_seq_len > 64 and heads==96 and kv_cache_hit_rate >= 0.6: choose fused
```
Matt: looks safe. Any regression risk on long-context generative workloads?
Alana: runbook: gate this behind a rollout flag and canary on dedicated pools. I also added a telemetry metric `kernel_fallback_rate_by_template` to track when we fall back to slow path.
perf-bot: perf dashboard created: https://perf.internal/redwood/fg-37455 :eyes: (snapshot id fg-37455, compare: baseline vs current)
Kai: longer term: refine kernel selector feature vector to include `kv_hit_rate_estimate`, `template_bucket`, `head_dim`, `hidden_size`, `rope_theta_scale`. we can train a small decision tree using current telemetry.
Jess: agree. also check model-specific defaults — Mixtral & Mistral families have different rope scaling expectations; we shouldn't bake a one-size default into the selector.
Alana: action items:
- (Alana) roll out selector change behind flag + canary (today)
- (Kai) add `kv_hit_rate` estimator to runtime (this sprint)
- (Jess) add chat_template tagging in router (this week)
- (Matt) monitor perf dashboard, watch p95 and `kernel_fallback_rate_by_template`
Everyone: reactions? :thumbsup:
Matt: :thumbsup:
Kai: :thumbsup:
Jess: :thumbsup:
Alana: thanks — will post rollout status in this thread when canary completes.
